title: Transfer a uniform annihilator bound through affine sheafification
statement: Let X be affine Noetherian, J ideal sheaf data, A=Γ(X,⊤), I=J(⊤), and L=tilde followed by pullback along X≅Spec A. For arbitrary A-modules T,P, a linear map ψ:T→P, an X-module G and an isomorphism ε:L(P)≅G, if I^t annihilates the algebraic kernel and cokernel of ψ, then the sheaf kernel and cokernel of L(ψ) followed by ε are annihilated by the shared sheaf ideal power J^t. No finiteness assumption and no positivity assumption on t are needed.

source.place: Tag 0889(1), affine construction, using Schemes Tags 01I7, 01IB, 01IC

proof.text: Use the existing private theorem AlgebraicGeometry.tilde_preservesKernel from Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.AffineDerivedTildeHomologyComparison, made available by a proof-only import all. That theorem proves kernel preservation by lifting the quasi-coherent kernel fork and reflecting its limit; no duplicate proof is introduced here. Restriction along the affine scheme isomorphism preserves limits; its natural comparison with pullback transfers this preservation to pullback. Both tilde and pullback are left adjoints and preserve cokernels. Thus the sheaf kernel and cokernel, also after postcomposition with epsilon, are isomorphic respectively to L of the algebraic kernel and quotient by the range, using ModuleCat.kernelIsoKer, ModuleCat.cokernelIsoRangeQuotient, PreservesKernel.iso, PreservesCokernel.iso, kernelCompMono and cokernelCompIsIso.

For any A-module M compute the global sections of L(M): restrict back along X.isoSpec.inv, replace pullback by restriction, and use restrictFunctorComp, restrictFunctorCongr and restrictFunctorId to identify this sheaf with tilde(M). Compose tilde.isoTop with this comparison on global sections and sectionsRestrictFromSpecLinearEquiv for the top affine open. The equality IsAffineOpen.fromSpec_top supplies the final chart identification. This yields an A-linear equivalence M with Gamma(X,L(M)), without a choice of arbitrary data. The two associated sheaves are quasi-coherent by quasi-coherence of tilde and pullback, and so are their isomorphic kernel and cokernel.

Compose these linear equivalences with evaluation of the kernel and cokernel isomorphisms. A linear equivalence preserves the annihilator (LinearEquiv.annihilator_eq). Apply idealPowerProduct_isZero_iff_affine_cover to the singleton cover consisting of the top affine open. The assumed two annihilator inequalities therefore give the two zero ideal-power products. No positivity or finiteness assumption is used, and the same singleton cover is valid for the empty scheme.

lean.statement:
theorem affine_map_annihilation_sheafification
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsAffine X] (J : X.IdealSheafData) :
    let A := Γ(X, ⊤)
    let I := J.ideal ⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top X⟩
    let L := tilde.functor A ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pullback X.isoSpec.hom
    ∀ (T P : ModuleCat.{u} A) (ψ : T →ₗ[A] P) (G : X.Modules)
      (ε : L.obj P ≅ G) (t : ℕ),
      I ^ t ≤ Module.annihilator A ψ.ker →
      I ^ t ≤ Module.annihilator A (P ⧸ ψ.range) →
      IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι t).2
        (kernel (L.map (ModuleCat.ofHom ψ) ≫ ε.hom))) ∧
      IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι t).2
        (cokernel (L.map (ModuleCat.ofHom ψ) ≫ ε.hom)))
